newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas off in winter, otherwise stable and thin.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas off in winter, otherwise stable and thin.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices softened slightly next winter and in the gas year starting from October, traders and brokers said, but the movements were marginal and the volume of trade was lower than in recent days.

The gas year from October was the most actively traded period, with at least four trades done at between 12.325 pence and 12.35 pence a therm. There were also rumours heard that a further trade was done at 12.25 pence a therm, but at least one trader and one broker were sceptical that this was done.

The first quarter was traded at 15.90 pence a therm, the bottom end of Tuesday's assessed range, and by the close the quarter had edged down to be offered at 15.95 pence against bids at 15.85 pence. There were rumours that the Q4/Q1 strip traded twice, at 14.15 pence and 14.20 pence, although these were not confirmed.

There were also some large volumes traded on the prompt market. One large buyer, frequently active on the prompt market, bought 680,000 therms on the day ahead market at 9.45 pence and 200,000 therms a day in the first half of July as well as 100,000 therms on the within day market.

But traded volumes were not as great as in some recent days. Dealers said there was little fundamental change to the market and no particular drivers behind prices which remained stable in many periods apart from the slight weakness next winter. "It's gone very quiet. lacklustre," said one trader.

Futures prices moved in line with OTC levels, stable in some months and slightly lower in others. The largest fall in a traded month was in March 1998, which slipped by 0.15 pence a therm. The total volume, 180 lots in 10 separate deals, was higher than in recent days.
